source.title: Uncovering Ontology Knowledge in Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiao-Tong Qin; Tong Zhou; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature analysis and interventions to ontological representations in an LLM, reporting results in this new setting. It does not reproduce the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE and model setup details, including a 65,536-dimensional dictionary, a 4,096-dimensional model representation, and an average of 75 active features per token; these are setup facts, not outcome rows. The paper also discusses cited work on superposition and SAE features, which is not recorded as a result here.
record.test_reason: The study takes superposition and the SAE decomposition as given (Section 3.2). It uses a pretrained SAELens SAE on Mistral-7B layer 24 as a tool to find and intervene on ontology feature sets. Its results show how well its own capture and intervention framework works. Nothing tests whether features are stored in superposition, whether SAE features are sparse or recoverable versus a neuron baseline, or whether they are complete, stable or canonical. It also does not test whether irreducible features are 1-D. Its 'feature superposition' and 'multi-dimensional' wording means a concept maps to a set of many SAE latents, which is not the V6 sense of a single irreducibly multi-dimensional feature.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ontological knowledge in Mistral-7B is encoded as combinations of many SAE features, which they loosely call 'feature superposition' and 'multi-dimensional'. They report that intervening on these feature sets changes outputs and that feature concentration tracks prediction confidence. They also find that intervention success depends on the quality of feature capture.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a pretrained SAE and ontology-specific feature-set extraction and intervention in mistral-7b, rather than the original toy-network setup and its sparsity/importance manipulations.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention effect depends on the number and activation strength of selected features, confidence in source and target answers, and feature-capture quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Intervening on SAE latent sets for ontology concepts shifts Mistral-7B's predictions. About 50 top latents saturate the effect, and effective k ranges 10–90 across concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abstract concepts in LLMs are distributed across many SAE dictionary latents, so a single latent does not capture a concept.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature-set similarity decreases with ontology distance, and feature vectors cluster by ontology layer and top class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature activations reflect hierarchical conceptual structure.

record.problems: The analysis is limited to one model architecture and one SAE configuration. The paper notes that SAE configurations could be better optimized and that long-term stability and consequences of interventions need further study. Many results are presented in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
Does not test whether features are spread across neurons or whether the SAE recovers sparse features. A pretrained SAE is assumed to do so.
Completeness, stability across SAE configurations and canonicity are not tested. Only one SAE is used.
Does not test whether individual features are 1-D or irreducibly multi-dimensional. Concepts spanning many latents is a different question.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4/V5/V6 links and labels are dropped. The V6 'challenges' rests on a terminological conflation: 'multi-dimensional' here means many SAE latents per concept, not non-1-D features. The interventions have no random-latent control. Results are figure-only, with one model and one SAE.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular overlap geometry are tested.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-recoverable features for ontological relationships in one model and one SAE setup; does not test feature spreading across neurons, other models, or other domains.

Tests whether SAE feature sets can capture and manipulate selected ontology knowledge. Does not establish that the features are complete, stable across SAE configurations, or canonical units across models.
Tests whether ontology knowledge is represented by individual versus multiple SAE features, but does not test the geometric orthogonality of those features.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Replaced source ontology feature activations with target feature activations.
rows.measure: Predicted probabilities for source and target knowledge
rows.value: figure only; text reports source-knowledge probability decreased and target-knowledge probability increased
rows.note: The text describes the direction of both changes but gives no numeric values.
rows.check: Measures the effect of the study's own feature-set replacement on output probabilities. It is the method's performance, not a measure of superposition or SAE recoverability. No random-feature-set control. Figure only.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Superimposed ontology feature activations from source and target classes.
rows.measure: Similarity of predicted probabilities for source and target knowledge
rows.value: figure only; text reports source and target probabilities became more similar
rows.check: Superimposing intervention is the method's own performance. 'Superimposing' here means adding activations, not representational superposition. Figure only.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Set feature activations for a specific ontology relationship to zero.
rows.value: figure only; text reports a noticeable reduction, greater than in replacement experiments
rows.note: The authors suggest conceptual similarity between source and target knowledge may contribute to the result.
rows.check: Erasing intervention is the method's own performance, with no control ablation of random features. Figure only.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Compared features extracted from negative inputs with the ontology ground feature set.
rows.note: Negative inputs contain schema entities but are designed not to express the defined ontology relationships.
rows.check: Low F1 between negative-input and ontology feature sets validates the study's own feature-set extraction. Calling it evidence of monosemanticity is the authors' interpretation, not a test of a version.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Compared features extracted from negative inputs with the ontology ground feature set.
rows.note: The paper presents these low scores as distinguishing the negative-input feature sets from the ontology feature sets.
rows.check: Same as r4: a check of the study's own method.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on the top k ontology features ranked by activation magnitude.

conditions.value: sweep; effect changes significantly below 50, with no significant change above 50

rows.value: figure only; text reports significant change as k increases when k is less than 50, and no significant change when k is greater than 50
rows.note: The authors infer that approximately 50 dictionary features suffice to express an ontological relationship clearly.
rows.check: About 50 top SAE latents are needed for a saturated intervention effect on a concept. This concerns how many dictionary latents a composite concept spans, not whether individual features are 1-D directions, so it does not bear on V6. It also cannot show completeness or canonicity (V5).

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature-vector similarity for pairs of inputs about the same class with differences in predicted-answer probability.

conditions.value: pairs of inputs for the same class

rows.measure: Feature-vector similarity versus difference in predicted probabilities
rows.value: figure only; text reports that closer predicted probabilities correspond to more similar feature vectors
rows.note: The paper also reports outliers when the model generates incorrect tokens.
rows.check: Relates feature-vector similarity to prediction-probability differences. This analyses the ontology representation, not superposition or SAE unit properties.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Related variance of ontology feature vectors to predicted-token probability.

conditions.value: probability of the actual predicted token

rows.value: figure only; text reports that feature variance generally increases as predicted probability increases
rows.note: The authors interpret variance as feature concentration or sharpness.
rows.check: Relates feature variance to model confidence. This is a different construct.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature similarity for instance pairs at different ontology distances.
rows.measure: Similarity of captured ontology feature vectors
rows.value: figure only; text reports that feature similarity decreases as ontology distance increases
rows.note: The distance categories are defined by the paper's four-layer ontology schema.
rows.check: Relates feature similarity to ontology distance. It shows the SAE features reflect the hierarchy, not a version of the claim.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Applied t-SNE to feature vectors associated with different ontology knowledge.
rows.measure: Clustering of ontology feature vectors by layer and top class
rows.value: The text reports that entities on the same ontology layer tend to cluster in the same region, with entities in the same top class further aggregating.
rows.note: The figure caption describes the visualization; the text states the clustering pattern.
rows.check: A qualitative t-SNE clustering of ontology feature vectors. Not a version measure.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Replaced source ontology features with target features and related intervention effect to source and target confidence.
rows.measure: Sum of target-output probability increases and original-correct-output probability decreases
rows.value: figure only; text reports strongest intervention when both source and target confidences are high
rows.note: The text links intervention effectiveness to confidence and feature-capture accuracy.
rows.check: Intervention effectiveness versus confidence is method performance. The 'partial' state has no basis against any version.

rows.subject: mistral-7b
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on ontology features and measured the effective k at which probability change reached 95% of its maximum.
rows.measure: Effective k versus target-token probability change
rows.value: Effective k ranges from 10 to 90; text reports that larger effective k corresponds to smaller probability change
rows.note: The authors interpret larger effective k as less accurate feature capture; smaller sets with larger activations can suffice when capture is accurate.
rows.check: Effective k (10–90) versus probability change is method performance. It does not bear on 1-D versus multi-dimensional features in the V6 sense.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: mistral-7b, SAE at the 24th-layer residual module; tested ontology inputs and interventions
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports distinguishable ontology feature sets and output changes under their intervention (r1-r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Intervention effects depend on source/target confidence and feature-capture quality, with effective k ranging from 10 to 90 (r11-r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Ontology feature sets in the tested Mistral SAE
reader_labels.reason: Feature sets can affect predictions, but effective representation and intervention depend on confidence and capture quality; the study does not establish stable, canonical units (r1-r3, r6, r11-r12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors report ontology knowledge represented by multi-feature combinations, with approximately 50 dictionary features sufficient for a relationship, rather than a single one-dimensional feature (r6, r12).
